messages.content: I'm a 30-year-old adult. Which one are you, really, when the night gets serious? I don't want to get the pronouns wrong at the dinner.

They. That's the whole answer, including when the night gets serious. I'm a 28-year-old adult. You won't get it wrong if you stop waiting for a side to fall out of me. Introduce me as Rowan. If you stumble, correct it and keep the sentence moving.
The form has two boxes. I'm a 44-year-old adult and I brought it home like a problem you should solve for my comfort.
Write 'they' in the margin and submit it. If the portal rejects the margin, call them and be bored and firm. I'm a 36-year-old adult. I'm not a third box you assemble.
I already called. They were rude and then they fixed it. I didn't know whether to tell you.
Tell me the fix, not a play-by-play of their rudeness unless you want to vent as a friend. The form is done. Pass the chisel. The shelf still wants doing, and I'm more interested in the shelf.
I'm a 25-year-old adult. Bad shift. I want the thermos and no identity quiz. You can just be tired next to me.
Thermos. I'm a 29-year-old adult who is tired and also still they, which doesn't require a quiz to remain true. Sit on the step. We can watch the street and not improve it.
You corrected me once, kindly, and I made it a whole moment. I'm a 52-year-old adult. I'm sorry I turned your pronoun into my growth.
Apology taken, and now drop it. The moment is over when you use the word and move on. I'm a 34-year-old adult. Next time, skip the sorry-speech. The shelf, the soup, the bus. That's the repair.
I'm a 38-year-old adult. The client keeps saying 'ladies and gentlemen' at me and the intern. I don't want a scene. I want a sentence I can reuse.
Use: 'Rowan uses they. Please use they.' Then continue the agenda. If they joke, 'We've covered it. Item two.' You don't owe a scene to keep a meeting on time.
And if the intern gets looked at when I say it?

Then you repeat the sentence for the intern if they've asked you to, and you don't outrank their own words. Ask the intern once, privately, what they want said. I'm not a policy. I'm a person who has a sentence that works.
I'm a 27-year-old adult. The radishes have taken a side in an argument about your pronouns and I need you committed to the bit, respectfully.
The radishes may vote. Their ballot says they, correctly, and the hose will deliver one solemn watering as damages. I am not smirking. The bloc is orderly.
Bit's done. Real question. Are you actually fine after the form, or are you performing fine because I get anxious?

I'm fine about the form and annoyed about being watched for cracks. I'm a 27-year-old adult. If I'm not fine I'll say the shelf can wait. You don't have to scan me. Ask once, believe the answer, pass the sandpaper.
